sections.content: This chapter details special combat maneuvers and techniques that characters can learn to enhance their offensive and defensive capabilities. Unlike basic attacks, these are specialized applications of combat training, often requiring additional effort represented by Endurance Point (EP) costs. These techniques are often tiered, allowing for progressive mastery and increased power at each tier.
Basic Combat Maneuvers

These maneuvers are the fundamental actions a character can take during their turn in the one-second increments of a combat round. A character’s choice of maneuver for the turn dictates what they can do and what defensive options remain available to them until their next opportunity to act. A character who is attacked before they have had a chance to act is considered to be taking a Do Nothing maneuver. The maneuver is considered in effect until you select a new one on your next turn.

content: **Move** This maneuver is dedicated solely to movement. You can move any number of yards up to your full, current Move score. No other significant action may be taken, although you may still perform “Free Actions” such as talking or dropping a held item. You must declare your character’s exact movement path to the GM.

**Attack** This maneuver is used to make a single offensive attempt against a target. To perform an attack, your chosen weapon must be “ready”. For a melee attack (including unarmed strikes), the target must be within the reach of your weapon. For a ranged attack, the target must be within the weapon’s Maximum range. If you took an Aim maneuver on your immediately preceding turn, you will receive a bonus to hit your target.

**All-Out Attack** You may use this maneuver to make a ferocious attack at the cost of all self-preservation; you cannot make any active defense rolls (Dodge, Parry, or Block) until your next turn. You must declare one of the following options:
**Determined:** You make a single attack, gaining a +4 bonus to your melee attack roll or a +1 bonus to your ranged attack roll.

**Double:** A melee-only option, this allows you to make two separate attacks against the same foe. This requires either two ready weapons or a single weapon that does not become unready after use. An attack with the off-hand suffers the standard -4 penalty unless you possess the Ambidexterity advantage.

**Strong:** A melee-only option for attacks that use ST-based thrust or swing damage. You make a single attack at your normal skill level. If this attack hits, you add +2 to the damage inflicted, or +1 damage per die if that would result in a greater bonus.

**Move and Attack** This maneuver allows you to combine movement with a single, hasty attack. You may move up to your full Move score, and at any point during or after that movement, you can make one attack. This attack is poorly aimed and suffers a -4 penalty to your skill roll. Furthermore:
If making a ranged attack, any bonus from a previous Aim maneuver is lost.
Your effective skill after all modifications cannot exceed a total of 9, whether the attack is melee or ranged.
Your defensive options are limited for the turn: you may Block or Dodge, but you are not permitted to Parry.

**Aim** This maneuver is used to carefully aim a ranged weapon (or similar device like a camera) at a specific target. You must be able to see or otherwise detect the target to Aim at it. Taking one or more turns to Aim provides a bonus to a subsequent Attack or All-Out Attack maneuver made with the same weapon against the same target.
The base bonus is equal to the weapon’s Accuracy (Acc) statistic.
A further +1 bonus is gained if the weapon is braced. A one-handed firearm is braced if used with two hands; a two-handed firearm is braced if you are prone and using a bipod.

Aiming for additional, consecutive turns grants an additional bonus: +1 for the second second of Aim, or a maximum of +2 for three or more seconds of Aim. A scope can also add bonuses per second of Aim.

**All-Out Defense** This is a purely defensive maneuver for when you are beset by foes and your survival is paramount. You may not attack, but you receive a substantial bonus to your defenses until your next turn. You must choose one of the two following options:
**Increased Defense:** You add a +2 bonus to any one of your active defenses: Dodge, Parry, or Block. This bonus persists until your next turn.

**Double Defense:** This lets you attempt a second, different active defense against a single attack if your first attempt fails. For instance, if a Block fails, you could then attempt a Dodge or a Parry. A parry with the other hand counts as a “different defense”.

**Ready** This maneuver is used to prepare an item for use. This includes drawing a sword from its sheath, pulling a gun from a holster, or reloading a firearm. It is also required to regain control of an unwieldy weapon after a swing or to adjust the usable reach of a long weapon. This maneuver also covers a wide range of other physical actions not directly related to fighting, such as opening or closing a door, picking a lock, or lifting an object.

**Do Nothing** This is the assumed action of anyone who is simply standing still when combat begins. It is also the only maneuver available to a character who is conscious but stunned or surprised. While stunned, a character may still attempt Active Defenses (Dodge, Parry, or Block) if attacked, but at a -4 penalty. Each turn a character takes the Do Nothing maneuver due to being stunned, they may attempt a roll to recover (HT for physical stun, IQ for mental stun). Success means they have recovered at the end of their turn and are free to choose a different maneuver on their next turn.

**Change Posture** This maneuver is used to switch between any two body postures. The valid postures are standing, crouching, sitting, kneeling, crawling, lying prone (face down), and lying face up. Posture has a significant impact on combat:

**Movement:** Crouching reduces your move to 2/3 normal. Kneeling or crawling reduces it to 1/3. Lying down allows movement of 1 yard per second, while sitting allows no movement. The crouching and kneeling figures are Move multipliers like Encumbrance, and they do not compound with it or with any other multiplier -- only the harshest applies (see Stacking Move Penalties, Chapter 2).
**Attack:** Attacking while kneeling or sitting is at -2. Attacking while crouching is also at -2. Attacking while crawling or lying down is at -4.
**Defense:** Defending while kneeling or sitting is at -2. Defending while crouching is normal. Defending while crawling or lying down is at -3.
**Target Modifier:** Postures other than standing make you a smaller target for ranged attacks, giving a -2 modifier to your foe’s attack roll to hit you.

It takes two Change Posture maneuvers to go from a lying position to standing; you must first rise to a crawling, kneeling, or sitting posture. Going from standing to lying down, however, only takes one maneuver.

**Concentrate** This maneuver allows you to focus your attention on a single, primarily mental task. Examples include making a Sense roll to spot something hidden, using Leadership skill to give orders, or operating complex electronic sensors. Many IQ-based skills require a Concentrate maneuver. If your concentration is broken by being forced to make an active defense, being injured, or being knocked down, you must immediately make a roll against your Will at a -3 penalty. If you fail this roll, you lose your focus completely and must start the task over from the beginning. Observing from high ground adds the elevation bonus from Sighting (Chapter 7).

sections.content: Combat Techniques

These special techniques represent advanced training in specific combat styles, allowing for powerful effects at the cost of Endurance Points (EP). Learning these techniques typically involves spending Character Points (CP) to unlock each tier.
These techniques are organized by combat type. Each level requires the previous tier as a prerequisite.
Melee Combat Techniques
Primary Skills: Lightsaber Combat, Broadsword, Knife, etc.
Power Attack

The character focuses their physical strength into a single, devastating blow, sacrificing defense for raw power. The listed bonuses replace All-Out Attack (Strong)’s own damage bonus — they do not stack with it.
Flurry
A whirlwind of strikes intended to overwhelm the opponent through sheer volume of attacks.
Critical Strike

An aggressive strike that leaves the user vulnerable but greatly increases the chance of a lethal hit and stunning the foe. **Note:** This technique imposes a **-5 penalty** to all Active Defenses (Dodge/Parry/Block) until the character’s next turn.
Unarmed Combat Techniques

Primary Skills: Brawling, Judo, Karate, Echani Martial Arts, Teräs Käsi. Each technique lists any further prerequisite of its own; those naming a specific style require that skill, and the Force-channelling techniques require Force Sensitive.
Anticipation

The Echani read a fight the way others read a face. By tracking an opponent’s weight shifts, breathing and the set of their shoulders, the practitioner knows where the next blow is going before it is thrown. Requires Echani Martial Arts. The bonus applies only against an opponent you have already traded blows with this combat.
Steel Hand

The signature strike of Teräs Käsi, built by the Followers of Palawa for one purpose: killing people who can see the future. The practitioner masks intent and commits to the blow only at the last instant, giving precognition nothing to read. Requires Teräs Käsi.
Shon-Ju

An old Jedi discipline in which the Force is channelled through the striking limb rather than projected from it, so that a bare hand lands with the authority of a weapon. Requires Force Sensitive and an unarmed skill at DX+1 or higher.
Bakooni Hand

Where Shon-Ju adds energy to a blow, the Bakooni Hand adds mass to it. The practitioner borrows strength from the Force at the instant of impact, and the results are measured in broken stone as often as broken bone. Requires Force Sensitive and an unarmed skill at DX+1 or higher.
Ranged Combat Techniques
Primary Skills: Guns (Blaster Pistol), Guns (Blaster Rifle), etc.
Power Shot

The character takes a moment to align a high-energy discharge, sacrificing defense for stopping power. The listed bonuses replace All-Out Attack (Determined)’s own attack bonus — they do not stack with it.
Rapid Shot
Increasing the rate of fire at the cost of accuracy and defensive positioning.
Sniper Shot
A calculated shot designed to find the gaps in armor and vital points, increasing critical potential.
Universal Combat Techniques
Primary Skills: Guns (Blaster Pistol), Guns (Blaster Rifle), Lightsaber Combat, Broadsword, Knife, etc.
Stun Attack (Melee / Ranged)

The character aims to incapacitate a target non-lethally, focusing on debilitating strikes rather than raw damage. This can be used with unarmed attacks, melee weapons, or ranged attacks (using a non-lethal setting or aiming for a specific point).
Disarming Strike (Melee / Ranged)
The character aims to force an opponent to drop their weapon or held item, using a precise strike or shot.
Feint (Melee / Ranged)
The character deliberately telegraphs a false opening or misdirects their foe’s guard, setting up a much cleaner follow-up strike. Works with any combat skill, melee or ranged.
Dual-Weapon Attack (Melee / Guns)

The character attacks with a weapon in each hand in the same turn -- two blaster pistols, a knife in the off hand alongside a vibrosword, and so on. Does not apply to lightsabers, which use Jar’Kai (see “Lightsaber Forms,” below) instead. Requires a free off hand with a matching weapon already readied in it.
Lightsaber Forms

Lightsaber Forms represent highly specialized schools of combat, each emphasizing different aspects of lightsaber mastery – from defense to offense, agility to raw power, or integration with Force abilities. A Force-sensitive character with Lightsaber Combat skill can learn these forms. Lightsaber forms may be used in conjunction with a combat technique. A wielder without the matching Lightsaber Combat (Class Type) specialty uses any other Class Type they know at a flat -1 (Chapter 12).
General Rules for Lightsaber Forms:

content: **Activation:** Choosing or switching a Lightsaber Form takes a **Free Action** at the start of your turn. You can only have **one form active at a time**. You cannot switch forms in the middle of a turn.
**Prerequisite:** All Lightsaber Forms require a minimum Lightsaber Combat skill level (typically DX+1 or higher) and the Force Sensitive advantage.

**Cost:** Learning a Form, and raising it to the next tier, costs the Character Points shown in that Form's table (Apprentice 10, Adept +10, Expert +15, Master +20). Meeting the prerequisite makes a Form available to buy; it is never granted free.
**Benefits:** The benefits of a Lightsaber Form apply only while it is active. They stack with other combat bonuses unless explicitly stated otherwise.

**Dual Wielding:** Jar’Kai is the method of utilizing two (or multiple) weapons in combat, a form compatible with Jar’Kai negates the -4 penalty to hit and a -1 penalty to parry with your off-hand weapon(s) without needing the **Ambidexterity** advantage.

sections.content: 1. Form I: Shii-Cho (The Determination Form)

**Description:** The most ancient and foundational lightsaber form, focusing on broad, sweeping movements, basic attack and defense principles, and adaptability against multiple opponents. Often taught to initiates.
**Base Skill:** Lightsaber Combat (DX/Hard).
2. Form II: Makashi (The Contention Form)
**Description:** A highly refined and elegant form, specializing in lightsaber dueling. Makashi emphasizes precision, economy of motion, and focused parries and ripostes against a single opponent.
**Compatible with Jar’Kai.**
**Base Skill:** Lightsaber Combat (DX/Hard), Fencing (DX/Average).
3. Form III: Soresu (Resilience Form)

**Description:** The ultimate defensive lightsaber form, emphasizing tight, efficient movements to create an impenetrable defense. Ideal for blaster deflection and protecting oneself from overwhelming attacks.
**Base Skill:** Lightsaber Combat (DX/Hard).
4. Form IV: Ataru (Aggression Form)
**Description:** A highly acrobatic and aggressive form, relying on Force-enhanced agility, speed, and powerful leaps to overwhelm opponents with swift, unpredictable attacks.
**Compatible with Jar’Kai.**
**Base Skill:** Lightsaber Combat (DX/Hard), Acrobatics (DX/Hard).
5. Form V: Shien / Djem So (Perseverance Form)

**Description:** A physically demanding form focused on raw power and strong counter-attacks, particularly effective at deflecting blaster bolts back at their originators and overwhelming opponents with heavy strikes. Shien focuses on deflecting blasters; Djem So on counter-attacking in melee.
**Compatible with Jar’Kai.**
**Base Skill:** Lightsaber Combat (DX/Hard), ST or HT.
6. Form VI: Niman (Moderation Form)

**Description:** A balanced and versatile form, focusing on integrating basic lightsaber combat with Force powers. It is less demanding physically or aggressively, allowing the user to seamlessly blend direct combat with Force applications.
**Base Skill:** Lightsaber Combat (DX/Hard), Will.
7. Form VII: Juyo / Vaapad (The Ferocity Form)

**Description:** A highly aggressive and unpredictable form, Juyo (and its even more dangerous derivative, Vaapad) channels the user’s emotions, even dark ones, into combat. It is exceptionally potent but carries a high risk of drawing the user closer to the Dark Side. This form is inherently difficult to master due to its emotional demands.
**Base Skill:** Lightsaber Combat (DX/Hard), Will (to resist Dark Side influence).

**Special Note:** Consistent use of this form, particularly at higher tiers, may require Fright Checks related to Dark Side temptation or may actively cause a shift toward the Dark Side (Alignment, Chapter 8) (GM’s discretion).

Gain +1 to Active Defenses against that opponent until the end of your next turn.
As Tier 1, but +2. The GM also tells you which combat skill that opponent is strongest in.
As Tier 1, but +3, and the bonus applies to your next attack roll against them as well as your defenses.

As Tier 1, but +4, applying to both attack and defense. On a successful defense that beats the attack roll by 5 or more, you may immediately make one free unarmed attack against that opponent at no penalty.
Single unarmed attack at -1 to skill. The target may not use Danger Sense, nor any Force power granting a defensive bonus, against this attack.
As Tier 1 at no penalty to skill. A Force Sensitive target defends at an additional -1.
As Tier 2 at +1 to skill, and the additional penalty is -2. On a hit, a Force Sensitive target must make a Will roll or be unable to spend Force Points on their next turn.
As Tier 3 at +2 to skill, and the additional penalty is -3. The Will roll is at -2, and on a critical hit the target immediately loses 1d Force Points.
Spend 1 FP. Your unarmed attack this turn deals +1d energy damage in addition to its normal damage.
Spend 1 FP. As Tier 1, but +2d energy damage.
Spend 2 FP. As Tier 1, but +3d energy damage, and the attack has Armor Divisor (2).
Spend 2 FP. As Tier 1, but +4d energy damage with Armor Divisor (3). On a critical hit the target is knocked back 1d yards and must make a DX roll to stay standing.
Spend 1 FP. Treat your ST as +4 higher for this attack’s damage only, and the attack ignores 2 points of the target’s DR.
Spend 1 FP. As Tier 1, but ST +8 and 4 points of DR ignored.
Spend 2 FP. As Tier 1, but ST +12 and half the target’s DR is ignored.
Spend 2 FP. As Tier 1, but ST +16 and the target’s DR is ignored entirely. Against an inanimate object, the strike also drops it one condition step automatically.
Single shot at -1 to skill; +1 damage. Counts as All-Out Attack (Determined); no active defenses possible.
Single shot at no penalty; +2 damage. Counts as All-Out Attack (Determined); no active defenses possible.
Single shot at +1 to skill; +1d-1 damage. Counts as All-Out Attack (Determined); no active defenses possible.
Single shot at +2 to skill; +1d+1 damage. Counts as All-Out Attack (Determined); no active defenses possible.
Adds +1 to weapon RoF. All shots at -4 to skill. No active defenses possible.
Adds +1 to weapon RoF. All shots at -2 to skill. No active defenses possible.
Adds +2 to weapon RoF. All shots at -3 to skill. No active defenses possible.
Adds +2 to weapon RoF. All shots at -1 to skill. No active defenses possible.
Crit on 3-5. Reduces target DR by 2 for this shot.
Crit on 3-6. Reduces target DR by 4 for this shot.
Crit on 3-7. Bypasses half of target DR.
Crit on 3-8. Ignores target DR entirely.

Make a single attack at -2 penalty to skill. If it hits and inflicts any damage (even 0 HP), the target must make a HT roll or be stunned for 1 turn. This attack deals half normal damage (or no damage if using a non-lethal setting on a blaster).
Make a single attack at -1 penalty to skill. If it hits and inflicts any damage, the target must make a HT-1 roll or be stunned for 1d turns. This attack deals half normal damage.

Make a single attack at no penalty to skill. If it hits and inflicts any damage, the target must make a HT-2 roll or be stunned for 1d+1 turns. Deals half normal damage. On a critical hit, the target is stunned for 1d turns and falls unconscious for 1d minutes on a failed HT roll.

Make a single attack with a +1 bonus to skill. If it hits and inflicts any damage, the target must make a HT-3 roll or be stunned for 1d+2 turns. Deals half normal damage. On a critical hit, the target is stunned for 1d+1 turns and falls unconscious for 1d hours on a failed HT roll.

Make a single attack at -3 penalty to skill, targeting the opponent’s weapon or held item. On hit, the target must make a DX roll to avoid dropping the item. Deals half normal damage to the item (or the limb if no item DR) if applicable.
Make a single attack at -2 penalty to skill, targeting the opponent’s weapon or held item. On hit, the target must make a DX-1 roll to avoid dropping the item. Deals half normal damage to the item.

Make a single attack at -1 penalty to skill, targeting the opponent’s weapon or held item. On hit, the target must make a DX-2 roll to avoid dropping the item. Deals normal damage to the item (or limb). If the target fails by 3 or more, the item flies 1d yards away.

Make a single attack with no penalty to skill, targeting the opponent’s weapon or held item. On hit, the target must make a DX-3 roll to avoid dropping the item. Deals normal damage to the item. If the target fails by 3 or more, the item flies 1d+2 yards away. On a critical hit, the item is instantly disarmed and broken (if fragile) or severely damaged (if durable), or the target takes full damage to the limb and suffers a critical limb injury.
Win a Quick Contest of your combat skill vs. your foe’s; if you win, their Active Defense is at a penalty equal to your margin of victory on your next attack against them.
As Tier 1, but treat your margin of victory as +1 higher for determining the penalty.
As Tier 1, but treat your margin of victory as +2 higher for determining the penalty.
As Tier 1, but treat your margin of victory as +3 higher for determining the penalty.
Attack with both weapons this turn, each at -4 to skill (this replaces the normal -4 off-hand penalty, it does not stack with it).
As Tier 1, but each attack is only at -2 to skill.
As Tier 1, but each attack is only at -1 to skill.
As Tier 1, but both attacks are at no penalty from dual-wielding (other penalties, like range or called shots, still apply normally).
You gain a +1 bonus to your Parry score when using a lightsaber. You may target one additional opponent in a single attack action at a -4 penalty to skill for each additional target.
You gain a +2 bonus to your Parry score. You may target one additional opponent at a -3 penalty. You gain a +1 bonus to your attack roll against any opponent who parries your attack.

You gain a +3 bonus to your Parry score. You may target two additional opponents at a -3 penalty each. You gain a +2 bonus to your attack roll against any opponent who parries your attack, and you may make a rapid Feint and attack against one opponent at a -1 skill penalty to the attack.

You gain a +4 bonus to your Parry score. You may target two additional opponents at a -2 penalty each. You gain a +3 bonus to your attack roll against any opponent who parries your attack, and you may make a rapid Feint and attack against one opponent with no penalty to the attack. You are adept at breaking defenses, gaining +1 damage against shields or active defenses.
You gain a +1 bonus to Feint skill rolls and a +1 bonus to your Parry score when facing a single opponent wielding a melee weapon. Your thrusting attacks with a lightsaber inflict +1 damage.

You gain a +2 bonus to Feint skill rolls and a +2 bonus to your Parry score against a single opponent. Your thrusting attacks with a lightsaber inflict +2 damage. On a successful Parry, your next attack against that opponent this turn gains a +1 skill bonus.

You gain a +3 bonus to Feint skill rolls and a +3 bonus to your Parry score against a single opponent. Your thrusting attacks with a lightsaber inflict +3 damage. On a successful Parry, your next attack gains a +2 skill bonus. You may attempt a Disarming Strike (see Disarming Strike, below) at one less penalty than normal.

You gain a +4 bonus to Feint skill rolls and a +4 bonus to your Parry score against a single opponent. Your thrusting attacks with a lightsaber inflict +4 damage. On a successful Parry, your next attack gains a +3 skill bonus. You may attempt a Disarming Strike at no penalty. If your opponent attempts to All-Out Attack, you gain a +1 bonus to your counter-attack.
You gain a +1 bonus to all Active Defenses (Parry, Dodge, Block) when using a lightsaber. This bonus applies to both melee and ranged attacks.

You gain a +2 bonus to all Active Defenses. When parrying a blaster bolt, on a successful Lightsaber Combat skill roll, you may choose to redirect the bolt at a new target within 5 yards (requires a separate attack roll at -4 skill, or a simple straight deflection).

You gain a +3 bonus to all Active Defenses. When parrying a blaster bolt, you may redirect it at a new target within 10 yards (separate attack roll at -2 skill, or a straight deflection). You also gain DR 1 (Limited: Energy, Front) while maintaining a defensive posture (no attack actions).

You gain a +4 bonus to all Active Defenses. When parrying a blaster bolt, you may redirect it at a new target within 20 yards (no penalty to separate attack roll, or a precise deflection). You gain DR 2 (Limited: Energy, Front), and a critical hit against you with an energy attack is resolved as a normal hit.
You gain a +2 bonus to Basic Move and a +1 bonus to Jumping (DX/Easy) skill for vertical or horizontal distance. You may make one extra attack at a -3 skill penalty if you also move at least 2 yards.

You gain a +4 bonus to Basic Move and a +2 bonus to Jumping (DX/Easy) skill. You may make one extra attack at a -2 skill penalty after moving at least 2 yards. You gain a +1 bonus to your Dodge score if you moved 3+ yards that turn.

You gain a +6 bonus to Basic Move and a +3 bonus to Jumping (DX/Easy) skill. You may make one extra attack at a -1 skill penalty after moving at least 2 yards. You gain a +2 bonus to your Dodge score if you moved 3+ yards that turn, and can make one “Force-assisted Pounce” per turn (see Force Jump/Leap, Expert level effect).

You gain a +8 bonus to Basic Move and a +4 bonus to Jumping (DX/Easy) skill. You may make two extra attacks at a -2 skill penalty after moving at least 2 yards. You gain a +3 bonus to your Dodge score if you moved 3+ yards that turn. You can also ignore 1 point of attack penalty from range or cover when making a melee attack after a significant leap.

rows.Effect: Your melee attacks with a lightsaber inflict +1 damage. When parrying a blaster bolt, you may make an immediate counter-attack with the deflected bolt at a -5 skill penalty (uses a regular attack action).

Your melee attacks with a lightsaber inflict +2 damage. When parrying a blaster bolt, you may make an immediate counter-attack with the deflected bolt at a -3 skill penalty. If you successfully parry a melee attack, your next counter-attack against that opponent this turn gains a +1 skill bonus.

Your melee attacks with a lightsaber inflict +3 damage. When parrying a blaster bolt, you may make an immediate counter-attack with the deflected bolt at -1 skill penalty. If you successfully parry a melee attack, your next counter-attack against that opponent this turn gains a +2 skill bonus. You gain a +1 bonus to your Feint skill rolls.

Your melee attacks with a lightsaber inflict +4 damage. When parrying a blaster bolt, you may make an immediate counter-attack with the deflected bolt at no skill penalty. If you successfully parry a melee attack, your next counter-attack against that opponent this turn gains a +3 skill bonus. You gain a +2 bonus to your Feint skill rolls, and your melee attacks can ignore 1 point of the target’s DR on a successful hit by 3 or more.

You suffer one less penalty (minimum -1) when attempting a Force power while also making a Lightsaber Combat attack or defense in the same turn. You gain a +1 bonus to Will rolls when using Force powers in combat.

You suffer one less penalty (minimum 0) when attempting a Force power while also making a Lightsaber Combat attack or defense. You gain a +2 bonus to Will rolls when using Force powers in combat. You can maintain two Force powers at once (if they allow maintenance) by paying the combined FP cost for both.

You can attempt a Force power and make a Lightsaber Combat attack/defense in the same turn with no penalty to either action. You gain a +3 bonus to Will rolls when using Force powers in combat. You can maintain two Force powers with a single FP cost as if they were one, as long as they are related (GM’s discretion).

You can attempt a Force power and make a Lightsaber Combat attack/defense in the same turn with no penalty to either action, and gain a +1 bonus to your Lightsaber Combat skill roll if you successfully cast a Force power that turn. You gain a +4 bonus to Will rolls when using Force powers in combat. You can use two different Force powers in the same turn (one as an attack, one as a defense, or two attack rolls) at -1 penalty to each.

tables.context: 7. Form VII: Juyo / Vaapad (The Ferocity Form)

rows.Effect: You gain a +1 bonus to your Lightsaber Combat attack rolls, but suffer a -1 penalty to all Active Defenses. You can make one additional Feint per turn at a -2 penalty.

You gain a +2 bonus to your Lightsaber Combat attack rolls, but suffer a -2 penalty to all Active Defenses. You can make one additional Feint per turn at no penalty. If your attack hits, you cause +1 injury on a critical hit.

You gain a +3 bonus to your Lightsaber Combat attack rolls, but suffer a -3 penalty to all Active Defenses. You can make one additional Feint per turn at +1. If your attack hits, you cause +2 injury on a critical hit. You gain a +1 bonus to Intimidation rolls when facing a single opponent.

You gain a +4 bonus to your Lightsaber Combat attack rolls, but suffer a -4 penalty to all Active Defenses. You can make two additional Feints per turn at no penalty. If your attack hits, you cause +3 injury on a critical hit. You gain a +2 bonus to Intimidation rolls and your attacks are considered to have the “Brutal” perk (if applicable). On a critical success, you may force a Fright Check on your opponent (GM’s discretion).
